source.title: Irish News, 19 May 1949, p. 3 ("Rural council nominations")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Londonderry (Derry) rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. Two contests were nominated; John S. Browne (U.) withdrew in Middle Liberties, leaving Patrick G. Coyle returned unopposed. Only Ardmore was actually polled. The eleven unopposed members added from the nominations lists (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1949, p. 6; Derry Journal, 18 May 1949), Tamnaherin from the Derry Journal list; full names checked against the Returning Officer's notice (Derry Journal, 8 June 1949, p. 1) (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Anti-Partitionist. Mr. John S. Browne (U.) withdrew his nomination after the nominations were lodged. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Middle Liberties' to Liberties Middle (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (LIBERTIES MIDDLE) spell it Liberties Middle. This round was filed under the spelling 'Middle Liberties', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (middle-liberties) answers with a redirect to this one.
